about: Answer keys for the five fictional case-study businesses: the 8 planted gaps in each profile's 'What is actually true' section, the controls that should catch each one, and 'evidence': a phrase that must appear in at least one of those controls' 'check' step in data/assessment.json for the gap to count as covered by the question bank.

01.text: Guest Wi-Fi, POS and CCTV on one flat network; router admin still default
DVR default admin password with remote viewing over the internet
POS admin PIN on a sticky note; former staff still have POS logins
Loyalty list collected with no notice; promos sent without consent
Staff IC and bank photos in the owner's phone gallery, syncing to a personal cloud without 2-step verification
Shared laptop with no Windows password; Google account always signed in
No CCTV signage or retention period
Nothing backed up outside the one Google account

02.text: Server PC on out-of-support Windows; clinic system not updated in 3 years
Backup disk always plugged into the server; restore never tested
Shared 'frontdesk' login; locum uses the lead doctor's login
Vendor remote-access tool always on, unattended, password never changed
Shared webmail without 2-step verification, password on a card; years of lab results
Lab results and IC photos sent over personal WhatsApp
No notice or consent for sensitive data; no process for patients asking for their records
No incident plan; nobody knows the breach notification duty

03.text: Founders and freelancer share one social/seller login; password reused
03.evidence: one login used by several people

03.text: 2-step verification off on the social account that owns the ad account and card
03.evidence: security settings of each key account

03.text: Previous freelancer still has full admin rights
Order exports in Downloads and in an 'anyone with the link' cloud folder
Printed packing lists with addresses go in the normal bin
Website admin account on a founder's personal email
Privacy notice copied from another shop, naming a different business
No agreement with the freelancer about protecting customer data

04.text: No MFA on cloud email; legacy sign-in allowed
04.evidence: security settings of each key account

04.text: NAS admin and shares reachable from the internet; firmware 2 years old
Client portal and banking logins in passwords.xlsx readable by all staff
No check on 'our bank account has changed' requests
Interns' and remote staff's personal laptops unencrypted and unmanaged, with client files synced
NAS snapshots only; no offsite or offline backup
Former staff mailboxes kept; one former intern's account never disabled
No retention rule: closed clients' IC copies kept 15+ years

05.text: Registration form asks for far more than needed (parents' IC numbers, medical notes)
Registration spreadsheet shared with all tutors as editors, including leavers; one public link
Photos and results of minors posted without consent; take-down request ignored
Video-call links reused weekly and posted in public-facing groups
Tutors message students directly on personal phones with no rules
Owner's personal email without 2-step verification used for all business logins
Former students' data never deleted (8 years)
Shared office PC with no password; browser saves every password
